title: Network intrusion detection system: A systematic study of machine learning and deep learning approaches
authors: Zeeshan Ahmad; Adnan Shahid Khan; Cheah Wai Shiang; Johari Abdullah; Farhan Ahmad
contribution: Taxonomy of ML/DL techniques for NIDS with a review of strengths/limitations of recent approaches
key_findings: Synthesizes trends in ML/DL-based NIDS across methodology, evaluation metrics, and dataset choice; no new experimental results
limitations: Survey scope, not an experimental study -- not evaluated on rigor/artifact dimensions with primary-study standards

title: Machine Learning for Anomaly Detection: A Systematic Review
authors: Ali Bou Nassif; Manar Abu Talib; Qassim Nasir; Fatima Dakalbab
thematic_class: Survey: ML for anomaly detection across domains
contribution: Broad SLR of ML models for anomaly detection covering applications, techniques, metrics, and datasets
key_findings: Reviews 290 articles (2000-2020); identifies 43 application areas and 29 distinct ML models; unsupervised methods most commonly adopted
limitations: Broad anomaly-detection scope beyond network intrusion specifically; dataset/metric comparability not harmonized across surveyed studies

title: Performance Analysis of Machine Learning Algorithms in Intrusion Detection System: A Review
authors: T. Saranya; S. Sridevi; C. Deisy; Tran Duc Chung; M.K.A. Ahamed Khan
contribution: Comparative evaluation of LDA, CART, and Random Forest for intrusion classification
key_findings: Reports comparative efficiency of LDA/CART/Random Forest classifiers on the KDD-CUP dataset
limitations: Relies on the outdated KDD-CUP dataset; no adversarial/evasion threat model considered

title: An Explainable Machine Learning Framework for Intrusion Detection Systems
authors: Maonan Wang; Kangfeng Zheng; Yanqing Yang; Xiujuan Wang
contribution: First reported use of SHAP for IDS explanation, combining local and global explanations across one-vs-all and multiclass classifiers
key_findings: SHAP-based framework improves interpretability of IDS decisions on NSL-KDD; compares one-vs-all vs. multiclass classifier explanations
limitations: Evaluated on a single dataset (NSL-KDD); no adversarial-evasion threat model

title: Benchmarking of Machine Learning for Anomaly Based Intrusion Detection Systems in the CICIDS2017 Dataset
authors: Ziadoon Kamil Maseer; Robiah Yusof; Nazrulazhar Bahaman; Salama A. Mostafa; Cik Feresa Mohd Foozy
contribution: Systematic benchmark of 31 ML-AIDS models on CICIDS2017 with training/testing time as an efficiency dimension
key_findings: k-NN, DT, and NB-based AIDS models obtain the best web-attack detection results among the 31 models compared; reports both accuracy and time-complexity metrics
limitations: Single dataset (CICIDS2017, itself class-imbalanced); no adversarial robustness evaluation

title: How Machine Learning is Revolutionizing Intrusion Detection
venue: Designing a Machine Learning Intrusion Detection System
contribution: Practitioner-facing overview of how ML techniques are applied to intrusion detection design
key_findings: Not a primary empirical study; frames motivations and design considerations for ML-based IDS rather than reporting new results
limitations: No experimental evaluation, no stated artifact or dataset; engaged as background/context rather than primary evidence per README Stage 4 guidance

title: Machine Learning for Intrusion Detection
contribution: Chapter-level introduction to applying deep learning methods to intrusion detection
key_findings: Introductory/overview content; no abstract available at screening time to extract quantitative findings from
limitations: No abstract/full-text metadata retrieved at screening time; full-text review needed to confirm scope and rigor

title: Intrusion Detection Systems based on Machine Learning
venue: Proceedings of the 2nd International Conference on Big Data, Modelling and Machine Learning
contribution: Evaluates machine learning classifiers for intrusion detection in a big-data/modelling conference setting
key_findings: No abstract retrieved at screening time; full text confirms classifier-comparison scope (see extraction notes)
limitations: Conference-length paper; likely limited experimental scale relative to a journal-length study

title: Trustable machine learning for intrusion detection systems
contribution: Proposes a CVSS-informed evaluation metric for IDS and studies decision-explainability and robustness to novel attacks
key_findings: Develops a cybersecurity-aware evaluation metric based on CVSS scores; explores explainability and detection of previously unseen attack types
limitations: Single-author thesis; French-language full text; not peer-reviewed in the journal/conference sense

title: Intrusion Detection using Machine Learning
venue: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)
contribution: Applies machine learning classifiers to intrusion detection
key_findings: No abstract retrieved at screening time; full text needed to confirm specific algorithms/dataset used
limitations: Venue does not enforce the same peer-review rigor as an indexed journal; full-text quality check needed before weighting findings heavily in synthesis

title: A Hybrid Deep Learning Anomaly Detection Framework for Intrusion Detection
authors: Rahul Kale; Zhi Lu; Kar Wai Fok; Vrizlynn L. L. Thing
contribution: Three-stage framework combining K-means clustering, GANomaly, and CNN for intrusion detection
key_findings: Evaluated across three benchmark datasets (NSL-KDD, CIC-IDS2018, TON_IoT); combines unsupervised, semi-supervised, and supervised stages to address limited labeled anomalous data
limitations: Preprint, not yet peer-reviewed; no adversarial-evasion evaluation reported in the abstract

title: Tree-based Intelligent Intrusion Detection System in Internet of Vehicles
authors: Li Yang; Abdallah Moubayed; Ismail Hamieh; Abdallah Shami
contribution: Tree-structure ensemble IDS with feature selection for autonomous-vehicle/IoV networks
key_findings: Reports high detection rate and low computational cost via ensemble learning plus feature selection on standard IoV attack datasets
limitations: Preprint; IoV-specific scope narrows generalizability to general NIDS

title: Cyber Situation Awareness with Active Learning for Intrusion Detection
contribution: Applies active learning and situation-awareness aggregation to reduce event-level alert volume and overfitting
key_findings: Moving from event-level alerts to system-level attack-probability aggregation improves detection accuracy and reduces alert volume on UNSW-NB15
limitations: Preprint; single dataset (UNSW-NB15); active-learning sampling strategy not compared against a full range of alternatives

title: Performance Comparison of Intrusion Detection Systems and Application of Machine Learning to Snort System
authors: Syed Ali Raza Shah; Biju Issac
thematic_class: Hybrid/optimized ML plug-in for signature-based IDS
contribution: Empirical Snort-vs-Suricata comparison at 10 Gbps plus an ML-optimized Snort adaptive plug-in (SVM + fuzzy logic + firefly algorithm)
key_findings: Best result: optimized SVM with firefly algorithm reaches FPR 8.6% and FNR 2.2%; Suricata processes higher throughput than Snort but consumes more compute
limitations: Preprint; single hardware/network setup (10 Gbps testbed only); comparison baseline restricted to two open-source IDS tools

title: LCCDE: A Decision-Based Ensemble Framework for Intrusion Detection in The Internet of Vehicles
authors: Li Yang; Abdallah Shami; Gary Stevens; Stephen De Rusett
contribution: Class-leader ensemble (LCCDE) selecting the best-performing model per attack class among XGBoost/LightGBM/CatBoost
key_findings: Demonstrated effective intrusion detection on both intra-vehicle (Car-Hacking) and external (CICIDS2017) network datasets using per-class model selection with confidence-based decisions
limitations: Preprint; two-dataset evaluation; per-class model-selection overhead not benchmarked against a single-model baseline
